title: judge scorer
description: A judge scorer: data/scorers/<scorer_id>.yaml, what judge-score reads. The sha256 of its content (the parsed YAML: a comment changes nothing) is recorded on every judged score, so an edit is a new scorer in effect: one that has made judged scores is not edited, a new version is a new scorer_id with `supersedes`. V13 names a judged score whose recorded hash is not the scorer's now, and adds the checks a schema cannot make (the prompt renders, judge ids are unique, a judge's system exists).

arms_match.description: The default arm set: a config_id substring.

supersedes.description: The scorer this one replaces: a changed rubric, prompt or judges is a new scorer (a frozen judging set is never rewritten), and this says which it follows (criteria drift, Shankar et al. 2024).

why.description: With supersedes: a sentence, what changed and why (which outputs led to it), carried like a promotion's reason.

mode.description: What a judge is asked: grade (each output scored on the scale), pick (name the best output of an item; outputs_per_call must cover every arm) or pairwise (which of two is better, every pair of arms; outputs_per_call is 2). Absent means grade.

system.description: Instead of params: the system (data/systems/<id>.yaml) this judge is, read as its settings under the record of the model it names, so the judge is called, priced and fingerprinted as the system is. Its settings must carry what params requires (provider, model, both prices) and the family.

params.description: A config's params for the judge model: called, priced and recorded as an arm's are, through the provider it names. Its keys are read as EVAL_JUDGE_<NAME> first, then <NAME>.

provider.description: Where the judge's calls go; fake calls nothing and can never be validated.

api_key_env.description: Another variable to read the key from. A credential, not part of the judge's identity.

family.description: The judge model's vendor family (vendor_a, openai, ...): a scorer needs judges from two families at least (ADR-0001 §4), which judge_score checks when it loads the scorer.

file.description: Relative to the scorer's directory, then the project.

sha256_at_16.description: The prompt rendered for 16 outputs, hashed: the bytes the validation measured.

listwise.description: Descriptive: what outputs_per_call > 1 means. Nothing reads it.

noise_check_fraction.description: Required and above 0: the judge's own noise is measured (ADR-0001 §4).

task.description: What is judged, when it is not SummEval's four dimensions on a 1-5 scale.

validation.description: The measurement that validates these judges for this use. Absent: the scorer is unvalidated and runs only with --unvalidated.

mode.description: The mode the judges were validated in; it must equal the scorer's mode. Absent means grade.
